adjudication_label: thermomechanical control of ordering and ductility
canonical_question: Why does aging outside the embrittlement-prone regime suppress excessive ordering and promote ductile interphase transition zones?

question_variants.question: Why does aging outside the embrittlement-prone regime suppress excessive ordering and promote ductile interphase transition zones?
question_variants.resolution_summary: Aging outside the embrittlement regime suppresses excessive ordering and promotes the formation of ductile interphase transition zones. This leads to brittle-to-ductile recovery.

answers.answer: Aging outside the embrittlement regime suppresses excessive ordering and promotes the formation of ductile interphase transition zones, facilitating brittle-to-ductile recovery.
answers.mechanism: suppressed excessive ordering, formation of ductile interphase transition zones
answers.boundary_limitation: Regime must be outside embrittlement-prone conditions
evidence_spans: Here, an unexpected ductile–brittle–ductile transition is discovered in a multiphase high‐entropy alloy (HEA) aged in an intermediate temperature regime.

Unlike the classical thermal embrittlement driven by grain boundary effects, this transition originates from the dynamic evolution of local chemical order (LCO) and phase boundary (PB) configurations in HEAs.

Aging within the embrittlement‐prone regime enhances chemical ordering, increases the density of ordered domains, and induces jagged PBs, collectively triggering plastic instability and the ductile−to−brittle transition.
